label: Gravity as geometry
dominant_mnemonic: Free motion follows curved spacetime geometry
icon_design: Simplify the detailed diagram to a curved grid with one gold natural path through it.
detail_design: Design the detailed graphic as a contrast between a flat fixed-background force picture and a curved spacetime geometry picture. The final geometry side should dominate: a free path follows the curved manifold rather than being pushed by a separate force arrow.
physics_idea: General relativity treats gravitational effects as spacetime geometry rather than a force field on a fixed background.
avoid: Newtonian-only apples, planets, rubber-sheet mass wells as the main motif, or suggesting that geometry is embedded in ordinary space.
icon_caption: A gold free path follows the curved spacetime geometry.
detail_caption: The detail graphic contrasts force-on-background intuition with GR's geometric view: free motion follows spacetime geometry.

label: Equivalence principle
dominant_mnemonic: Acceleration and gravity give the same local laboratory behaviour
icon_design: Simplify the detailed diagram to two small labs with matching falling-ball behaviour and a/g labels.
detail_design: Design the detailed graphic as two local laboratories: one accelerated upward, one in a uniform gravitational field. The internal ball behaviour should match, while the labels a and g identify the two descriptions being compared.
physics_idea: The equivalence principle says that uniform gravity and acceleration are locally indistinguishable in a sufficiently small laboratory.
avoid: Tidal stretching as the main feature, planets, global fields, or implying equivalence holds over large regions.
icon_caption: Two local laboratories show the same ball behaviour under a and g.
detail_caption: Acceleration and uniform gravity have the same local experimental signature; tidal effects are deliberately excluded from this small-lab picture.

label: Local inertial frame
dominant_mnemonic: A small flat SR frame attached to curved spacetime
icon_design: Simplify the detailed diagram to a curved patch with a small flat tangent frame carrying x and ct axes.
detail_design: Design the detailed graphic as a curved spacetime patch with a local flat plane at one event. Draw small x and ct axes on that plane so it reads as an SR-like local coordinate frame rather than a global inertial frame.
physics_idea: A local inertial frame recovers the SR form locally at one event in curved spacetime.
avoid: A global inertial grid covering the curved patch, tidal-free claims over a large region, or ordinary screen axes detached from the local plane.
icon_caption: A small x-ct frame sits on a local flat patch of curved spacetime.
detail_caption: SR is recovered locally: near one event the curved geometry has a small flat frame with x and ct axes.

label: Freely falling observer
dominant_mnemonic: Unsupported motion follows a natural spacetime path
icon_design: Simplify the detailed diagram to an observer moving along a blue free-fall path on curved spacetime.
detail_design: Design the detailed graphic as a freely falling observer following a natural curved-spacetime path. Add a secondary supported observer with an upward support cue only in the detail view, so the main idea remains unsupported inertial motion.
physics_idea: A freely falling observer has no non-gravitational support or thrust force and follows inertial motion in GR.
avoid: Rocket-thrust imagery as the main path, ordinary falling-object cartoons detached from spacetime, or implying standing still on a surface is free fall.
icon_caption: The observer follows a blue free-fall path without thrust.
detail_caption: Free fall is inertial motion in GR; the supported observer cue shows what free fall is not.

label: Tidal gravity
dominant_mnemonic: Nearby free-fall paths accelerate relative to each other
icon_design: Simplify the detailed diagram to three neighbouring free-fall paths with red relative-separation arrows.
detail_design: Design the detailed graphic as neighbouring freely falling worldlines that converge or diverge on a curved patch. Red arrows should show relative acceleration or stretching between paths. Keep tensor curvature notation out of this introductory graphic.
physics_idea: Tidal gravity is the relative acceleration of neighbouring freely falling bodies and is the operational sign of curvature.
avoid: A single falling object, uniform gravity alone, full Riemann tensor notation, or force arrows that do not compare neighbouring free-fall paths.
icon_caption: Neighbouring free-fall paths spread or converge under tidal gravity.
detail_caption: Tidal gravity is not one object's fall; it is relative motion between nearby freely falling paths, the first operational hint of curvature.

label: Weak-field metric
dominant_mnemonic: Nearly flat geometry with a small mass-induced perturbation
icon_design: Use a pale almost-rectangular grid gently distorted around a compact gold mass, with a small h label.
detail_design: Show an almost-flat coordinate grid whose lines bend only slightly near a compact source. In the detail version add g = eta + h and |h| much less than 1 so the perturbative split is explicit without turning the image into an equation card.
physics_idea: A weak gravitational field is represented by a metric that differs only slightly from flat spacetime.
avoid: A deep rubber-sheet well, strongly curved black-hole geometry, or a grid so distorted that the perturbation no longer looks small.
icon_caption: A nearly flat grid bends gently around a small source.
detail_caption: The weak-field metric is flat spacetime plus a small perturbation h produced by the source.

label: Newtonian limit
dominant_mnemonic: A shallow relativistic potential becoming Newtonian acceleration
icon_design: Use a shallow blue potential well, a gold test body, and one red downward acceleration arrow g.
detail_design: Draw a weak potential Phi with a test body accelerating down its shallow gradient. The detail version should state the slow-motion and weak-field assumptions and show g = -grad Phi, making the approximation conditions visible.
physics_idea: For weak fields and slow motion, the relativistic equation of motion reduces to Newtonian gravity in a potential Phi.
detail_labels: Phi, g, slow motion, weak field
avoid: Strong-field horizons, relativistic-speed trajectories, or an unexplained falling apple detached from the potential.
icon_caption: A test body accelerates down a shallow potential Phi.
detail_caption: Under weak-field and slow-motion assumptions, spacetime geometry reproduces Newtonian acceleration g = -grad Phi.

label: Gravitational redshift
dominant_mnemonic: Light climbing a gravitational field loses frequency
icon_design: Show a gold photon wave climbing from a blue lower emitter to a red upper receiver, with nu_e and nu_r.
detail_design: Place emitter and receiver at two gravitational heights and connect them with an upward travelling wave. The detail version should show nu_r < nu_e and a restrained background curvature cue so the frequency change reads as gravitational rather than Doppler shift.
physics_idea: A photon received higher in a static gravitational field has lower frequency than when emitted lower down.
avoid: Relative-motion Doppler diagrams, expanding-universe redshift, prisms, or changing the photon's path without showing the two gravitational heights.
icon_caption: An upward photon links a high-frequency emitter to a lower-frequency receiver.
detail_caption: Light climbing out of a gravitational field is received at lower frequency: gravitational redshift.

label: Light deflection
dominant_mnemonic: A null ray bending around mass
icon_design: Show one gold light ray curved past a central mass against a faint straight undeflected path.
detail_design: Draw incoming light, a compact mass M, and an outgoing ray deflected from the straight reference line. In the detail version mark a small angle alpha and add faint radial geometry rings without suggesting refraction by a medium.
physics_idea: Spacetime curvature around mass changes the path followed by light.
avoid: A glass lens as the physical cause, a light ray falling vertically, a black-hole capture orbit, or multiple decorative rays obscuring the single deflection.
icon_caption: A gold light ray bends away from its faint straight reference path near a mass.
detail_caption: The mass curves spacetime, so the light ray follows a deflected null path with angle alpha.

label: Perihelion precession
dominant_mnemonic: Successive orbital ellipses rotate their closest approach
icon_design: Show two differently oriented elliptical orbits around one gold mass, joined by a red advance arrow.
detail_design: Use two successive osculating ellipses with distinct colours and mark their perihelia. The detail version should connect each perihelion to the central mass and label the angular advance Delta varpi.
physics_idea: Relativistic corrections make an orbit's perihelion advance rather than repeat a closed Newtonian ellipse.
avoid: A circular orbit with no distinguished perihelion, wholesale orbital decay, frame dragging, or many loops too dense to read at icon size.
icon_caption: Two successive ellipses show the perihelion rotating around the central mass.
detail_caption: The closest-approach direction advances by Delta varpi from one orbit to the next.

label: Post-Newtonian approximation
dominant_mnemonic: Relativistic corrections organised by increasing order
icon_design: Show a rising three-step sequence labelled 0PN, 1PN, and 2PN.
detail_design: Build a clean approximation staircase from Newtonian 0PN through 1PN and 2PN. In the detail version label the successive inverse-c corrections and describe them as controlled relativistic corrections, not separate physical theories.
physics_idea: The post-Newtonian method expands relativistic gravity in systematically ordered corrections to Newtonian dynamics.
avoid: An accuracy progress bar with no expansion parameter, a quantum perturbation series, or implying that higher order always means stronger gravity.
icon_caption: A staircase orders Newtonian and successive post-Newtonian corrections.
detail_caption: Post-Newtonian bookkeeping adds controlled relativistic corrections order by order beyond Newtonian gravity.

label: Gravitational waves
dominant_mnemonic: Travelling tidal strain in weak geometry
icon_design: Show a blue sinusoidal wave crossing between four red test masses whose ring alternately stretches and squeezes.
detail_design: Draw a weak-field wave travelling horizontally through a small ring of freely falling test masses. Show the ring as dashed neutral positions plus red current positions in a plus-polarization stretch/squeeze pattern. The detail version should include h, plus/cross cues, and a wavefront arrow while avoiding dense waveform modelling.
physics_idea: Gravitational waves are propagating metric perturbations whose physical content is tidal strain between freely falling masses.
avoid: Sound-wave medium, water ripples, explosions, a generic coordinate wiggle without test masses, or implying spherical pulsation radiates.
icon_caption: A passing wave stretches one axis of a test-mass ring while squeezing the other.
detail_caption: The wave is seen through changing separations of freely falling masses: geometry carries a transverse tidal strain.

label: Schwarzschild metric
dominant_mnemonic: Static spherical vacuum geometry outside a mass
icon_design: Use concentric blue geometry rings and radial lines around one compact dark central mass.
detail_design: Show the exterior Schwarzschild geometry as a symmetric radial coordinate grid surrounding a compact source. The detail version should state static, spherical, and vacuum and label the radial coordinate without presenting a dense metric formula.
physics_idea: The Schwarzschild metric is the exact static, spherically symmetric vacuum geometry outside a non-rotating mass.
avoid: A rotating accretion disc, gravitational waves, a generic rubber sheet, or implying that the exterior vacuum contains distributed matter.
icon_caption: A spherical exterior grid surrounds a compact central mass.
detail_caption: The radial symmetry makes visible that the Schwarzschild exterior is static, spherical, and vacuum.

label: Schwarzschild radius
dominant_mnemonic: Mass defining a characteristic radius
icon_design: Show a gold mass inside a bold red radius ring with a radial arrow labelled r_s.
detail_design: Draw a central mass M and a clearly measured surrounding radius r_s. In the detail version add r_s = 2GM/c^2 and the phrase mass sets the scale; keep this about the length scale rather than horizon causality.
physics_idea: The Schwarzschild radius is the geometric length scale 2GM/c^2 associated with a mass.
avoid: Treating r_s as every object's material surface, showing one-way causal arrows, or conflating the scale directly with the central singularity.
icon_caption: A radial arrow measures the red Schwarzschild-radius ring around mass M.
detail_caption: The mass M fixes the Schwarzschild length scale r_s = 2GM/c^2.

label: Event horizon
dominant_mnemonic: A one-way causal boundary
icon_design: Use a bold circular boundary with red arrows entering and one green exterior arrow escaping.
detail_design: Represent the horizon as a global one-way causal boundary: future-directed cues cross inward, while only an exterior cue points away. Label r = r_s in the detail version and avoid depicting the boundary as a material shell or curvature explosion.
physics_idea: An event horizon separates events that can communicate with distant infinity from those that cannot.
avoid: A solid material surface, a red curvature singularity at the boundary, coordinate-grid failure as the main subject, or an object hovering exactly on the horizon.
icon_caption: Inward arrows cross the bold horizon while an exterior arrow can still escape.
detail_caption: The event horizon is a one-way causal boundary, not a material shell or local curvature singularity.

label: Coordinate singularity
dominant_mnemonic: A failing chart over regular geometry
icon_design: Show coordinate lines bunching at a dashed red horizon while one green path crosses smoothly.
detail_design: Draw a chart whose coordinate lines become crowded at r_s, contrasted with a regular physical path that continues through the same boundary. The detail view should label chart bunching, path crossing, and finite curvature.
physics_idea: A coordinate singularity is a failure of a particular chart, removable by using coordinates regular at the same geometry.
detail_labels: r_s, chart bunches, path crosses, finite curvature
avoid: A red central curvature blow-up, a path ending at the horizon, or implying that all coordinates become invalid there.
icon_caption: Crowded chart lines stop at r_s while a green path crosses the boundary.
detail_caption: The Schwarzschild chart fails at the horizon, but a regular path and finite curvature show that the geometry does not.

label: Black hole singularity
dominant_mnemonic: Future-directed interior paths ending on a spacelike singular boundary
icon_design: Show an interior region below a blue horizon, with red future paths ending on a jagged red lower boundary labelled r = 0.
detail_design: Label the lower boundary as spacelike and mark divergent K; keep the horizon visibly separate above it.
physics_idea: The Schwarzschild central singularity is a genuine geometric breakdown where curvature invariants diverge.
avoid: Putting the singularity at the horizon, drawing an ordinary point mass with regular interior, or suggesting a coordinate change can remove the invariant divergence. Do not depict it as a stationary spatial point or an explosion.
icon_caption: Interior futures end on the jagged r = 0 singular boundary.
detail_caption: The Schwarzschild singularity is a spacelike future boundary with divergent curvature, distinct from the regular horizon.

label: Effective potential for orbits
dominant_mnemonic: Orbital motion encoded by extrema and turning points
icon_design: Show the timelike potential for L/m = 4, with an inner maximum, outer minimum and an energy-squared line at radial turning points.
detail_design: Mark the inner maximum unstable and outer minimum stable; plot E-squared rather than E for the stated radial normalisation.
physics_idea: Conserved energy and angular momentum reduce Schwarzschild radial motion to an effective-potential problem.
detail_labels: V_eff, r, energy squared, stable, unstable
avoid: A Newtonian potential well with no relativistic extrema, a spacetime embedding diagram, or an orbit drawn without connecting it to turning points and stability.
icon_caption: An energy line cuts the effective-potential curve at radial turning points.
detail_caption: At fixed angular momentum, the inner maximum is unstable and the outer minimum stable; intersections with energy squared mark radial turning points.

label: Stress-energy tensor in GR
dominant_mnemonic: Energy density flux and stress packaged as one curved-spacetime tensor
icon_design: Show a T_mu_nu block containing epsilon, flux S, and stress sigma, with gold arrows leaving one face.
detail_design: Design a compact tensor block whose internal entries distinguish density, flux, and stress while outward arrows make transport visible. Add a subtle curved-spacetime cue only in the detail version so this remains a matter tensor rather than a curvature tensor.
physics_idea: Stress-energy packages local energy density, momentum density, flux, and stress as the source of spacetime curvature.
detail_labels: T_mu_nu, epsilon, S, sigma, density, flux, stress
avoid: A purely electromagnetic tensor, a dense component matrix, curvature symbols as the subject, or arrows with no tensor source.
icon_caption: A T_mu_nu block combines density, flux, and stress with outward transport arrows.
detail_caption: The stress-energy tensor packages observer-dependent densities and fluxes into one geometric source tensor.

label: Perfect fluid
dominant_mnemonic: Fluid density moving with four-velocity and equal pressure in all directions
icon_design: Show a blue circular fluid parcel, gold density dots, equal radial pressure arrows, and one green u vector.
detail_design: Draw a fluid element whose pressure arrows have equal length in every direction and whose internal matter is carried along one four-velocity u. In the detail view identify epsilon and state that pressure is isotropic.
physics_idea: A perfect fluid has rest-frame energy density and isotropic pressure but no viscosity, heat flow, or shear stress.
avoid: Shear arrows of unequal length, vortices, heat conduction, individual molecular collisions, or a static liquid with no four-velocity.
icon_caption: Equal blue pressure arrows surround a density parcel moving along u.
detail_caption: The fluid's local rest frame has density epsilon and the same pressure in every spatial direction.

label: Energy conditions
dominant_mnemonic: Testing stress-energy contractions against classical inequalities
icon_design: Show a blue T_mu_nu tile tested by timelike u and null k directions, producing a green nonnegative result.
detail_design: Present energy conditions as a test applied to stress-energy: observer or null directions contract with T and feed an inequality tile. The detail version must note that this is a classical assumption, not an identity.
physics_idea: Energy conditions impose selected nonnegative-density or causal-flow assumptions on stress-energy.
avoid: A universal law badge, quantum certainty, conservation arrows, or an inequality detached from an observer or null direction.
icon_caption: Observer directions test T_mu_nu and feed a green nonnegative result.
detail_caption: Energy conditions are additional classical assumptions about what observers or null directions measure.

label: Covariant conservation
dominant_mnemonic: Locally balanced energy-momentum flux in curved spacetime
icon_design: Show a curved blue region with matched gold boundary flux arrows and nabla_mu T^mu_nu = 0.
detail_design: Draw local energy-momentum flow through a curved-spacetime volume and centre the covariant-divergence equation. The detail view should describe local balance and subtly show why geometry-aware comparison is needed.
physics_idea: Covariant conservation states local energy-momentum balance while including the spacetime connection.
avoid: A claim of globally conserved gravitational energy, plain partial derivatives, a closed box with no flux, or arrows suggesting matter disappears.
icon_caption: Balanced boundary flux surrounds the covariant-divergence equation.
detail_caption: The vanishing covariant divergence expresses local energy-momentum balance on curved spacetime.

label: Equation of state
dominant_mnemonic: A constitutive curve relating pressure to energy density
icon_design: Show p and epsilon axes with a clean blue p(epsilon) curve and one highlighted state point.
detail_design: Draw pressure as a function of energy density with one sample thermodynamic state. In the detail version add the idealized linear form p = w epsilon and note that the relation closes the matter model.
physics_idea: An equation of state supplies material information relating pressure and energy density so the fluid-gravity equations close.
detail_labels: p, epsilon, p(epsilon), p = w epsilon
avoid: A gravitational field equation, temperature-only plot, phase diagram complexity, or implying one universal equation of state for all matter.
icon_caption: A highlighted state lies on the material relation p(epsilon).
detail_caption: The equation of state supplies the constitutive relation needed to close a fluid-gravity model.

label: Einstein field equations
dominant_mnemonic: Geometry coupled locally to stress-energy
icon_design: Show a blue curved-geometry tile equal to a gold stress-energy component tile.
detail_design: Place geometry G_mu_nu and matter T_mu_nu on equal visual footing, linked by an equals sign. The detail version should display the compact G - Lambda g = kappa T structure and label the two sides geometry and stress-energy.
physics_idea: Einstein's equations relate local spacetime curvature to the local stress-energy source.
detail_labels: G - Lambda g = kappa T, geometry, stress-energy
avoid: A scalar inverse-square law, a one-way force arrow from matter, a dense ten-equation component display, or geometry without a local source tensor.
icon_caption: A curved geometry tile balances a stress-energy tile across an equals sign.
detail_caption: Einstein's field equation is a local tensor balance between spacetime geometry and stress-energy.

label: Cosmological constant
dominant_mnemonic: A uniform metric term supporting vacuum curvature
icon_design: Show concentric blue rings expanding radially from a central red Lambda with no matter source.
detail_design: Use a symmetric empty-space motif with a central Lambda and uniform outward geometry arrows. The detail version should say uniform vacuum term and curved even with T = 0, avoiding claims about a specific microscopic origin.
physics_idea: The cosmological constant adds a uniform metric-proportional term that can curve spacetime without ordinary matter.
avoid: Matter particles as the cause, an exploding point, a measured cosmological history, or identifying Lambda unconditionally with one microscopic vacuum-energy model.
icon_caption: Uniform radial geometry arrows surround Lambda in otherwise empty space.
detail_caption: For positive Lambda, the cosmological term permits repulsive vacuum curvature even without ordinary matter.

label: Einstein-Hilbert action
dominant_mnemonic: Metric variation of a curvature action producing field equations
icon_design: Show an S_EH action tile varied by delta g into a green G_mu_nu result tile.
detail_design: Present the Einstein-Hilbert action as the input to a metric-variation operation. In the detail version hint at the negative integral of R + 2 Lambda and state stationary action to field equation, with a subtle curved-boundary cue.
physics_idea: Varying the gravitational curvature action with respect to the metric yields Einstein's equations, subject to proper boundary treatment.
detail_labels: S_EH, negative integral R + 2 Lambda, delta g, G_mu_nu
avoid: A path action for one particle, varying coordinates rather than the metric, hiding the curvature scalar, or suggesting boundary terms never matter.
icon_caption: Metric variation carries the S_EH tile into a geometric field-equation tile.
detail_caption: The Einstein-Hilbert action makes the metric dynamical: stationary metric variation yields the field equations.

label: Stress-energy from action variation
dominant_mnemonic: Matter action response to changing geometry
icon_design: Show a gold matter-action S_m tile perturbed by delta g and producing a blue T_mu_nu source tile.
detail_design: Draw the matter action with faint internal matter cues, followed by a metric-variation operation and a stress-energy result. The detail version should call T the source and describe it as matter's response to geometry.
physics_idea: Stress-energy is defined variationally by how the matter action changes under a metric variation.
avoid: A gravitational action producing G, a coordinate relabelling, force arrows, or a source tensor appearing without showing its action response origin.
icon_caption: A metric perturbation of S_m produces the source tensor T_mu_nu.
detail_caption: The variational definition makes stress-energy the response of matter action to a change in spacetime geometry.

label: Trace-reversed equations
dominant_mnemonic: Contracting and substituting to isolate Ricci curvature
icon_design: Show a G_mu_nu = kappa T_mu_nu tile passing through a trace arrow into a bold R_mu_nu tile.
detail_design: Make the algebraic operation visible: start with the Einstein form, contract to obtain the trace, and substitute to reach the Ricci form. The detail version should show the trace-adjusted source T_mu_nu - one-half g_mu_nu T and state that the physics is unchanged.
physics_idea: Trace reversal rewrites Einstein's equation equivalently as an equation directly for the Ricci tensor.
detail_labels: G_mu_nu = kappa T_mu_nu, trace, R_mu_nu, T_mu_nu - 1/2 g_mu_nu T
avoid: Erasing curvature, changing the physical theory, matrix transposition, or presenting the Ricci form without the trace operation.
icon_caption: A trace operation transforms the Einstein-tensor form into a bold Ricci-tensor form.
detail_caption: With zero cosmological constant, contracting and substituting the trace gives an equivalent Ricci form of the same field equations.

label: Vacuum field equations
dominant_mnemonic: Ricci-flat spacetime retaining tidal curvature
icon_design: Show an empty blue curved grid labelled T_mu_nu = 0 and R_mu_nu = 0.
detail_design: Draw a matter-free region whose grid remains visibly curved. The detail version should add two red neighbouring paths with relative convergence and state vacuum need not be flat, distinguishing Ricci-flatness from a zero Riemann tensor.
physics_idea: With vanishing ordinary stress-energy and Lambda, the vacuum equations require Ricci-flatness but can allow tidal curvature.
detail_labels: T_mu_nu = 0, R_mu_nu = 0, vacuum need not be flat
avoid: A blank featureless plane, claiming the full Riemann tensor vanishes, ordinary matter particles, or a cosmological-constant vacuum without stating conventions.
icon_caption: An empty but curved grid carries T_mu_nu = 0 and R_mu_nu = 0.
detail_caption: With zero cosmological constant, ricci-flat vacuum can still contain nonzero tidal curvature, as the converging paths emphasize.

label: Spacetime metric
dominant_mnemonic: Metric tensor carried by a curved spacetime patch
icon_design: Show a curved manifold grid with a central g tensor glyph.
detail_design: Place the metric glyph on a curved patch and add a measured interval cue. Label its roles in lengths, times, and angles.
physics_idea: The spacetime metric assigns invariant intervals and causal geometry.
avoid: A coordinate grid alone, curvature tensor, or Euclidean ruler detached from spacetime.
icon_caption: A g glyph sits on curved spacetime geometry.
detail_caption: The metric determines spacetime lengths, times, angles, and causal intervals.

label: Inverse metric
dominant_mnemonic: Metric and inverse contracting to the identity
icon_design: Show g_mu_nu multiplied by g^nu_rho to give delta.
detail_design: Use paired metric and inverse-metric tiles with a contraction and identity result. Add the raising and lowering role in the detail view.
physics_idea: The inverse metric undoes metric contraction and supports index raising.
avoid: A matrix inverse detached from tensor indices or implying a second independent metric.
icon_caption: Metric and inverse tiles contract to delta.
detail_caption: The inverse metric reverses metric contraction and raises indices.

label: Volume element
dominant_mnemonic: Invariant volume represented by a distorted coordinate cell
icon_design: Show a skewed coordinate grid with one highlighted local volume cell.
detail_design: Highlight one coordinate cell inside a distorted grid and label the invariant measure sqrt(-g) d4x in the detail view.
physics_idea: The metric determinant converts coordinate volume into invariant spacetime volume.
avoid: A flat unit cube with no metric factor or a spatial-only area element.
icon_caption: A highlighted cell sits inside a distorted coordinate grid.
detail_caption: The determinant factor converts a coordinate cell into an invariant volume element.

label: Line element
dominant_mnemonic: Metric interval between neighbouring events
icon_design: Show two red points on a curved patch joined by a gold ds-squared segment.
detail_design: Add ds^2 = g_mu_nu dx^mu dx^nu beneath the curved-patch interval.
physics_idea: The line element assigns an invariant infinitesimal interval.
avoid: A finite global distance or coordinate difference alone.
icon_caption: A gold ds-squared segment joins nearby events.
detail_caption: The metric turns coordinate displacement into invariant interval.

label: Proper time in curved spacetime
dominant_mnemonic: Clock ticks accumulated along a curved timelike path
icon_design: Show a black worldline on curved spacetime with blue tau ticks.
detail_design: Add the statement clock time along a timelike curve.
physics_idea: Proper time is the time recorded along a timelike worldline.
avoid: Coordinate time alone or a null path.
icon_caption: Blue ticks mark proper time along a curved worldline.
detail_caption: A clock accumulates tau along its timelike history.

label: Null curve
dominant_mnemonic: Light following a cone boundary with zero interval
icon_design: Show a gold light ray on the blue boundary of a light cone.
detail_design: Add ds^2 = 0 and a faint time axis.
physics_idea: A null curve has zero spacetime interval and carries lightlike influence.
avoid: A timelike massive path or light inside the cone.
icon_caption: A gold light path follows the cone boundary.
detail_caption: Null motion lies exactly on the causal cone with ds-squared zero.

label: Causal structure
dominant_mnemonic: Future and past cones organizing possible influence
icon_design: Show blue future and grey past cones meeting at one red event.
detail_design: Label future, past, and the exterior spacelike region.
physics_idea: Causal structure separates events that can influence one another from spacelike-separated events.
avoid: A single trajectory or an unlabelled geometric cone.
icon_caption: Future and past cones meet at one event.
detail_caption: The cones partition causal futures, pasts, and spacelike separation.

label: Local flatness
dominant_mnemonic: A small flat frame embedded in curved spacetime
icon_design: Show a curved patch containing a small green-edged flat coordinate square.
detail_design: Add g approaches eta at one event.
physics_idea: At any regular event the metric can be made locally Minkowskian.
avoid: A global flat grid covering all curved spacetime.
icon_caption: A small flat frame sits within a curved patch.
detail_caption: Curved spacetime is locally Minkowskian at a chosen event.

label: Metric signature convention
dominant_mnemonic: Two equivalent sign conventions requiring consistency
icon_design: Show +--- and -+++ tiles side by side.
detail_design: Label the time-positive and time-negative conventions and demand consistent use.
physics_idea: Metric signature chooses the relative signs of temporal and spatial directions.
avoid: Mixing conventions within one calculation or suggesting different physics.
icon_caption: Two signature tiles present the standard alternatives.
detail_caption: Either signature works when definitions and calculations remain consistent.

label: Connection
dominant_mnemonic: A rule comparing directions at nearby points
icon_design: Show tangent arrows along a curved path on a manifold patch.
detail_design: Use several nearby arrows and state that the connection supplies the comparison rule.
physics_idea: A connection defines differentiation and transport between tangent spaces.
avoid: A force field or globally fixed vector grid.
icon_caption: Tangent arrows follow a path across curved geometry.
detail_caption: The connection tells how to compare directions at neighbouring points.

label: Christoffel symbols
dominant_mnemonic: Coordinate coefficients of a connection
icon_design: Show a Gamma tile over a coordinate grid.
detail_design: Label Gamma with its indices and call it coordinate connection coefficients.
physics_idea: Christoffel symbols are coordinate-dependent coefficients of the Levi-Civita connection.
avoid: Treating Gamma as a tensor or curvature itself.
icon_caption: A Gamma tile sits on a coordinate chart.
detail_caption: Christoffel symbols encode the connection in a chosen coordinate system.

label: Covariant derivative
dominant_mnemonic: Vector change corrected for geometry
icon_design: Show vectors at two points and a green nabla V comparison.
detail_design: State ordinary change plus connection correction.
physics_idea: The covariant derivative measures tensor variation while correcting for changing bases.
avoid: A raw component difference with no connection.
icon_caption: Nearby vectors are compared by nabla V.
detail_caption: Covariant differentiation separates physical change from coordinate-basis change.

label: Metric compatibility
dominant_mnemonic: Transport preserving metric inner products
icon_design: Show equal ruler segments at two locations with nabla g = 0.
detail_design: State that transport preserves metric inner products.
physics_idea: Metric compatibility makes the connection preserve lengths and angles under transport.
avoid: Changing ruler lengths or a second metric.
icon_caption: Matching gold rulers accompany nabla g equals zero.
detail_caption: The compatible connection preserves metric comparisons during transport.

label: Torsion-free connection
dominant_mnemonic: An infinitesimal transport parallelogram closing
icon_design: Show a blue arrow parallelogram returning to its red start point.
detail_design: Label T = 0 and state that the infinitesimal parallelogram closes.
physics_idea: Vanishing torsion means the connection has no antisymmetric displacement defect.
avoid: A finite holonomy loop or curvature claim.
icon_caption: The transport parallelogram closes at its start.
detail_caption: Torsion-free transport has no infinitesimal closure defect.

label: Parallel transport
dominant_mnemonic: A vector carried around a curved loop
icon_design: Show green vectors transported along a blue loop on a manifold.
detail_design: Note that the rule is unchanged while loop holonomy can alter final orientation.
physics_idea: Parallel transport carries vectors using the connection without local turning.
avoid: Keeping screen orientation fixed or confusing transport with a force.
